// diagnostic E0324

Jet.AliasWithoutParameters

Type alias without type parameters over a plain type — use `distinct` for a distinct primitive name, or give a number its value

What

Type alias without type parameters over a plain type — use `distinct` for a distinct primitive name, or give a number its value

Why

At file level `name: Type` with no value names a type, and a transparent alias is only for shortening generic spellings: one with no type parameters names one application of a generic type, such as `Names: Set<String>`

Fix

Use `Name: distinct BaseType` for a distinct primitive name, add type parameters to the alias, or give a number constant its value (`LIMIT: Int{0}`).

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning Jet.AliasWithoutParameters: Tests/UI/bodiless_file_level_fn_is_a_function_type.stderr.

Error: Jet.AliasWithoutParameters: A type alias of a plain type needs type parameters — write `Name<T>: …`
  --> Tests/UI/bodiless_file_level_fn_is_a_function_type.jet:4:1
    |
  4 | Pick: fn(Int) -> Int
    | ^^^^
 Why: A transparent type alias is only for shortening generic spellings, so one without type parameters names a generic application such as `Set<String>`
 Fix: For a distinct type name over a primitive, use `Name: distinct BaseType` instead
